sources.title: Martin Taylor, Lectures on the nonlinear stability of the Schwarzschild family of black holes, complete lecture notes (Spring 2022)
sources.locator: Full 46-page PDF retrieved; §6.4, PDF pp. 40–41, was inspected. It places Aretakis derivative growth on extremal horizons and distinguishes this fixed-background linear result from open nonlinear stability questions; no RN equation or proof is imported.

source_resolution.argument: Defines the exact extremal ingoing dyonic RN background, its local horizon, and the regular C3 neutral spherical test-scalar class. It asserts no solution existence; ACω is inherited only through the metric-connection/tangent-bundle suppliers.

source_dispositions.locator: §1.1 supplies context for the fixed extremal RN scalar-wave setup; the exact metric and length convention are taken from the local mathematical supplier.
PDF pp. 9–11 give the ingoing chart and spherical wave equation; the local definition fixes the scalar operator and domain explicitly.
§6.4, PDF pp. 40–41, used only to preserve the distinction between linear fixed-background horizon behavior and nonlinear stability.

source_resolution.argument: Computes the inverse ingoing metric and volume density, reduces Box_g psi=0 for a spherical scalar, rewrites the equation for phi=r psi, evaluates it at the double-zero horizon, and applies the zero-derivative theorem. The conserved normalization is H=partial_r(r psi), equal to m times Aretakis's H0=partial_r psi+psi/m convention.

source_dispositions.locator: §12.1, Proposition 12.1.1, PDF p. 28, gives the independently derived spherical conserved charge in the normalization partial_r psi+psi/m.
§3, Proposition 3.0.1, PDF p. 8, provides continuation context; its broader global estimates are not used.
PDF pp. 9–10, independent calculation of the same spherical horizon charge.

source_resolution.argument: Differentiates the exact reduced equation once in r, obtains phi_rr,v=-H/m^2+phi(v,m)/m^3, and proves the decaying horizon-trace term has sublinear primitive by the mean value theorem. Uniqueness of primitives then yields phi_rr(v,m)/v→-H/m^2. The decay premise is explicit and is not proved from global initial data.

source_dispositions.locator: §2 Theorem 6 and §7.4, PDF pp. 7–8 and 31, are broader global results under the paper's data and decay assumptions; they are not used as proof premises.
PDF pp. 9–11 provide an independent decay-conditioned derivative-growth calculation; the local proof keeps the residual phi(v,m)/m^3 term and justifies its averaged limit.
§12.1, Proposition 12.1.1, PDF p. 28, supplies context for the conserved charge only.
§6.4, PDF pp. 40–41, supports the fixed-background scope warning and no nonlinear conclusion.

source_resolution.argument: Substitutes the explicit constant field psi=c≠0: Box_g psi=0, phi=cr, H=c, phi(v,m)=cm≠0, and phi_rr=0. It shows why the extra horizon-trace decay hypothesis cannot be omitted.
